ambiguities.text: The specification does not explicitly define the endianness of the 11-bit value extraction from hash bytes
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume big-endian byte ordering based on Ethereum convention where hash[0] is most significant. This needs verification against implementation.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'efficient searching of logs' is used without defining what constitutes efficient or the expected false positive rate
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume efficiency refers to O(1) bloom check vs O(n) log scan per block. False positive rate is mathematically determined by 2048-bit filter with 3 hash functions.

implicit_assumptions.description: The keccak256 hash function produces uniformly distributed outputs for the purposes of bloom filter bit distribution
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-uniform distribution could lead to higher false positive rates, degrading log search performance but not affecting correctness

implicit_assumptions.description: Log entries contain valid 20-byte addresses and 32-byte topics
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malformed log data could produce unexpected bloom filter values, potentially affecting log search accuracy

implicit_assumptions.description: The 256-byte (2048-bit) bloom filter size is sufficient for the expected number of log entries per block
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Excessive logs per block could saturate the bloom filter, causing all searches to return false positives and eliminating the search optimization
